title: Build an 8-bit bitwise XOR
statement_md: Create a module named `bitwise_xor8` with two 8-bit inputs `a` and `b` and one 8-bit output `y`. Each output bit is the XOR of the matching input bits. The logic is combinational, so `y` must follow the inputs whenever either of them changes.

tests.hint: Check that every output bit uses ^ (XOR), not | or +.

tests.purpose: passes a through when b is 0
tests.hint: XOR with zero should pass the other operand through unchanged.

tests.purpose: cancels to 0 when a equals b
tests.hint: XOR of identical operands must be zero in every bit position.

tests.purpose: sets every bit for complementary inputs
tests.hint: Check that every output bit uses ^, not | or +.

tests.purpose: keeps bit positions independent on a mixed pattern
tests.hint: Check which operator you used. Addition carries information between bit positions; XOR must not.

tests.purpose: changes only the bit that differs
tests.hint: Each output bit must depend only on the matching input bits, not on neighbouring bits.
The output must update whenever b changes, even if a stays the same. Avoid an incomplete sensitivity list.

hints: XOR compares one bit position at a time. Nothing should carry from one bit into the next.
A single continuous assignment covers all eight bits at once.
If you use an always block, make sure it reacts to both a and b.
